verses.zh: 那时，所罗门说：耶和华曾说他必住在幽暗之处。
verses.en: Then Solomon said, “The Lord has said that he lives in thick darkness.

verses.zh: 但我已经建造殿宇作你的居所，为你永远的住处。
verses.en: O Lord,[NOTE:1] I have built a lofty temple for you, a place where you can live permanently.”
notes: The words “O Lord” do not appear in the Hebrew text, but they are supplied in the translation for clarification; Solomon addresses the Lord in prayer at this point.

verses.zh: 王转脸为以色列会众祝福，以色列会众就都站立。
verses.en: Then the king turned around[NOTE:1] and pronounced a blessing over the whole Israelite assembly as they stood there.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “turned his face.”
Heb “and he blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.”

verses.zh: 所罗门说：「耶和华―以色列的　神是应当称颂的！因他亲口向我父大卫所应许的，也亲手成就了。
verses.en: He said, “The Lord God of Israel is worthy of praise because he has fulfilled[NOTE:1] what he promised[NOTE:2] my father David.
notes: The Hebrew text reads, “fulfilled by his hand,” but the phrase “by his hand” is somewhat redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
The Hebrew text reads, “promised by his mouth,” but the phrase “by his mouth” is somewhat redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 他说：『自从我领我民出埃及地以来，我未曾在以色列众支派中选择一城建造殿宇为我名的居所，也未曾拣选一人作我民以色列的君；
verses.en: He told David,[NOTE:1] ‘Since the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a temple in which to live.[NOTE:2] Nor did I choose a man as leader of my people Israel.
notes: Heb “saying.”

Heb “to build a house for my name to be there.” Here “name” is used by metonymy for the Lord himself, and thus the expression “to be there” refers to his taking up residence there (hence the translation, “a temple in which to live”). In this case the temple is referred to as a “house” where the Lord himself can reside.

verses.zh: 但选择耶路撒冷为我名的居所，又拣选大卫治理我民以色列。』」
verses.en: But now I have chosen Jerusalem as a place to live,[NOTE:1] and I have chosen David to lead my people Israel.’
notes: Heb “for my name to be there.” See also the note on the word “live” in v. 5.

verses.zh: 所罗门说：「我父大卫曾立意要为耶和华―以色列　神的名建殿，
verses.en: Now my father David had a strong desire to build a temple to honor the Lord God of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: On the significance of the Lord’s “name,” see the note on the word “live” in v. 5.tn Heb “and it was with the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.”

verses.zh: 耶和华却对我父大卫说：『你立意要为我的名建殿，这意思甚好；
verses.en: The Lord told my father David, ‘It is right for you to have a strong desire to build a temple to honor me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Because it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.”

verses.zh: 只是你不可建殿，惟你所生的儿子必为我名建殿。』
verses.en: But you will not build the temple; your very own son will build the temple for my honor.’[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your son, the one who came out of your body, he will build the temple for my name.”

verses.zh: 「现在耶和华成就了他所应许的话，使我接续我父大卫坐以色列的国位，是照耶和华所说的，又为耶和华―以色列　神的名建造了殿。
verses.en: The Lord has kept the promise he made. I have taken my father David’s place and have occupied the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised. I have built this temple for the honor of the Lord God of Israel

verses.zh: 我将约柜安置在其中，柜内有耶和华的约，就是他与以色列人所立的约。」
verses.en: and set up in it a place for the ark containing the covenant the Lord made with the Israelites.”

verses.zh: 所罗门当着以色列会众，站在耶和华的坛前，举起手来，
verses.en: He stood before the altar of the Lord in front of the entire assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

verses.zh: 〈所罗门曾造一个铜台，长五肘，宽五肘，高三肘，放在院中〉就站在台上，当着以色列的会众跪下，向天举手，
verses.en: Solomon had made a bronze platform and had placed it in the middle of the enclosure. It was 7½ feet[NOTE:1] long, 7½ feet[NOTE:2] wide, and 4½ feet[NOTE:3] high. He stood on it and then got down on his knees in front of the entire assembly of Israel. He spread out his hands toward the sky,
notes: Heb “5 cubits.” Assuming a cubit of 18 inches (45 cm), the length would have been 7.5 feet (2.25 m).
Heb “5 cubits.”
Heb “3 cubits.” Assuming a cubit of 18 inches (45 cm), the height would have been 4.5 feet (1.35 m).

verses.zh: 说：「耶和华―以色列的　神啊，天上地下没有神可比你的！你向那尽心行在你面前的仆人守约施慈爱；
verses.en: and prayed:[NOTE:1] “O Lord God of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven or on earth! You maintain covenantal loyalty[NOTE:2] to your servants who obey you with sincerity.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “said.”
Heb “one who keeps the covenant and the loyal love.”
Heb “who walk before you with all their heart.”

verses.zh: 向你仆人―我父大卫所应许的话现在应验了。你亲口应许，亲手成就，正如今日一样。
verses.en: You have kept your word to your servant, my father David;[NOTE:1] this very day you have fulfilled what you promised.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[you] who kept to your servant David my father that which you spoke to him.”
Heb “you spoke by your mouth and by your hand you fulfilled, as this day.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神啊，你所应许你仆人―我父大卫的话说：『你的子孙若谨慎自己的行为，遵守我的律法，像你在我面前所行的一样，就不断人坐以色列的国位。』现在求你应验这话。
verses.en: Now, O Lord God of Israel, keep the promise you made to your servant, my father David, when you said, ‘You will never fail to have a successor ruling before me on the throne of Israel,[NOTE:1] provided that your descendants watch their step and obey my law as you have done.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “there will not be cut off from you a man from before me sitting on the throne of Israel.”
Heb “guard their way by walking in my law as you have walked before me.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神啊，求你成就向你仆人大卫所应许的话。
verses.en: Now, O Lord God of Israel, may the promise you made to your servant David be realized.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “prove to be reliable.”

verses.zh: 「　神果真与世人同住在地上吗？看哪，天和天上的天尚且不足你居住的，何况我所建的这殿呢？
verses.en: “God does not really live with humankind on the earth![NOTE:1] Look, if the sky and the highest heaven cannot contain you, how much less this temple I have built!
notes: Heb “Indeed, can God really live with mankind on the earth?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course not,” the force of which is reflected in the translation “God does not really live with mankind on the earth.”

verses.zh: 惟求耶和华―我的　神垂顾仆人的祷告祈求，俯听仆人在你面前的祈祷呼吁。
verses.en: But respond favorably to[NOTE:1] your servant’s prayer and his request for help, O Lord my God. Answer[NOTE:2] the desperate prayer[NOTE:3] your servant is presenting to you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “turn to.”
Heb “by listening to.”
Heb “the loud cry and the prayer.”
Heb “praying before you.”

verses.zh: 愿你昼夜看顾这殿，就是你应许立为你名的居所；求你垂听仆人向此处祷告的话。
verses.en: Night and day may you watch over this temple, the place where you promised you would live.[NOTE:1] May you answer your servant’s prayer for this place.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “so your eyes might be open toward this house night and day, toward the place about which you promised to place your name there.”
Heb “by listening to the prayer which your servant is praying concerning this place.”

verses.zh: 你仆人和你民以色列向此处祈祷的时候，求你从天上你的居所垂听，垂听而赦免。
verses.en: Respond to the requests of your servant and your people Israel for this place.[NOTE:1] Hear from your heavenly dwelling place and respond favorably and forgive.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “listen to the requests of your servant and your people Israel which they are praying concerning this place.”
Heb “hear and forgive.”

verses.zh: 「人若得罪邻舍，有人叫他起誓，他来到这殿，在你的坛前起誓，
verses.en: “When someone is accused of sinning against his neighbor and the latter pronounces a curse on the alleged offender before your altar in this temple,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and if the man who sins against his neighbor when one takes up against him a curse to curse him and the curse comes before your altar in this house.”

verses.zh: 求你从天上垂听，判断你的仆人，定恶人有罪，照他所行的报应在他头上；定义人有理，照他的义赏赐他。
verses.en: listen from heaven and make a just decision about your servants’ claims. Condemn the guilty party, declare the other innocent, and give both of them what they deserve.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you, hear [from] heaven and act and judge your servants by repaying the guilty, to give his way on his head, and to declare the innocent to be innocent, to give to him according to his innocence.”

verses.zh: 「你的民以色列若得罪你，败在仇敌面前，又回心转意承认你的名，在这殿里向你祈求祷告，
verses.en: “If your people Israel are defeated by an enemy[NOTE:1] because they sinned against you, then if they come back to you, renew their allegiance to you,[NOTE:2] and pray for your help[NOTE:3] before you in this temple,
notes: Or “are struck down before an enemy.”
Heb “confess [or perhaps, “praise”] your name.”
Heb “and they pray and ask for help.”

verses.zh: 求你从天上垂听，赦免你民以色列的罪，使他们归回你赐给他们和他们列祖之地。
verses.en: then listen from heaven, forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to them and their ancestors.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 31, 38).

verses.zh: 「你的民因得罪你，你惩罚他们，使天闭塞不下雨，他们若向此处祷告，承认你的名，离开他们的罪，
verses.en: “The time will come when[NOTE:1] the skies[NOTE:2] are shut up tightly and no rain falls because your people[NOTE:3] sinned against you. When they direct their prayers toward this place, renew their allegiance to you,[NOTE:4] and turn away from their sin because you punish[NOTE:5] them,
notes: Heb “when.” In the Hebrew text vv. 26-27a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
Or “heavens” (also in v. 12). The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “they.”
Heb “confess [or perhaps, “praise”] your name.”

The Hebrew text reads “because you answer them,” as if the verb is from עָנָה (ʿanah, “answer”). However, this reference to a divine answer is premature, since the next verse asks for God to intervene in mercy. It is better to revocalize the consonantal text as תְעַנֵּם (teʿannem, “you afflict them”), a Piel verb form from the homonym עָנָה (“afflict”).

verses.zh: 求你在天上垂听，赦免你仆人和你民以色列的罪，将当行的善道指教他们，且降雨在你的地，就是你赐给你民为业之地。
verses.en: then listen from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Certainly[NOTE:1] you will then teach them the right way to live[NOTE:2] and send rain on your land that you have given your people to possess.[NOTE:3]
notes: The present translation understands כִּי (ki) in an emphatic or asseverative sense (“Certainly”). Other translations have “indeed” (NASB), “when” (NRSV), “so” (NEB), or leave the word untranslated (NIV).
Heb “the good way in which they should walk.”
Or “for an inheritance.”

verses.zh: 「国中若有饥荒、瘟疫、旱风、霉烂、蝗虫、蚂蚱，或有仇敌犯境，围困城邑，无论遭遇甚么灾祸疾病，
verses.en: “The time will come when the land suffers from a famine, a plague, blight, and disease, or a locust[NOTE:1] invasion, or when their enemy lays siege to the cities of the land,[NOTE:2] or when some other type of plague or epidemic occurs.
notes: Actually two Hebrew words appear here, both of which are usually (but not always) taken as referring to locusts. Perhaps different stages of growth or different varieties are in view, but this is uncertain. NEB has “locusts new-sloughed or fully grown”; NASB has “locust or grasshopper”; NIV has “locusts or grasshoppers”; NRSV has “locust, or caterpillar.”
Heb “in the land, his gates.”

verses.zh: 你的民以色列，或是众人，或是一人，自觉灾祸甚苦，向这殿举手，无论祈求甚么，祷告甚么，
verses.en: When all your people Israel pray and ask for help,[NOTE:1] as they acknowledge their intense pain[NOTE:2] and spread out their hands toward this temple,
notes: Heb “every prayer, every request for help which will be to all the people, to all your people Israel.”
Heb “which they know, each his pain and his affliction.”

verses.zh: 求你从天上你的居所垂听赦免。你是知道人心的，要照各人所行的待他们（惟有你知道世人的心），
verses.en: then listen from your heavenly dwelling place, forgive their sin,[NOTE:1] and act favorably toward each one based on your evaluation of their motives.[NOTE:2] (Indeed you are the only one who can correctly evaluate the motives of all people.)[NOTE:3]
notes: The words “their sin” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied for clarification.

Heb “and give to each one according to all his ways because you know his heart.” In the Hebrew text vv. 28-30a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided up for stylistic reasons.
Heb “Indeed you know, you alone, the heart of the sons of mankind.”

verses.zh: 使他们在你赐给我们列祖之地上一生一世敬畏你，遵行你的道。
verses.en: Then they will honor[NOTE:1] you by obeying you[NOTE:2] throughout their lifetimes as[NOTE:3] they live on the land you gave to our ancestors.
notes: Heb “fear.”
Heb “by walking in your ways.”
Heb “all the days [in] which.”

verses.zh: 「论到不属你民以色列的外邦人，为你的大名和大能的手，并伸出来的膀臂，从远方而来，向这殿祷告，
verses.en: “Foreigners who do not belong to your people Israel will come from a distant land because of your great reputation[NOTE:1] and your ability to accomplish mighty deeds;[NOTE:2] they will come and direct their prayers toward this temple.
notes: Heb “your great name.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor (thus the translation here, “your great reputation”).
Heb “and your strong hand and your outstretched arm.”

verses.zh: 求你从天上你的居所垂听，照着外邦人所祈求的而行，使天下万民都认识你的名，敬畏你，像你的民以色列一样，又使他们知道我建造的这殿是称为你名下的。
verses.en: Then listen from your heavenly dwelling place and answer all the prayers of the foreigners.[NOTE:1] Then all the nations of the earth will acknowledge your reputation,[NOTE:2] obey[NOTE:3] you as your people Israel do, and recognize that this temple I built belongs to you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and do all which the foreigner calls to [i.e., “requests of”] you.”
Heb “name.” See the note on “reputation” in v. 32.
Heb “fear.”
Heb “that your name is called over this house which I built.” The Hebrew idiom “call the name over” indicates ownership. See 2 Sam 12:28.

verses.zh: 「你的民若奉你的差遣，无论往何处去与仇敌争战，向你所选择的城与我为你名所建造的殿祷告，
verses.en: “When you direct your people to march out and fight their enemies,[NOTE:1] and they direct their prayers to you toward this chosen city and this temple I built for your honor,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “When your people go out for battle against their enemies in the way which you send them.”
Heb “toward this city which you have chosen and the house which I built for your name.”

verses.zh: 求你从天上垂听他们的祷告祈求，使他们得胜。
verses.en: then listen from heaven to their prayers for help[NOTE:1] and vindicate them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “their prayer and their request for help.”
Heb “and accomplish their justice.”

verses.zh: 「你的民若得罪你（世上没有不犯罪的人），你向他们发怒，将他们交给仇敌掳到或远或近之地；
verses.en: “The time will come when your people[NOTE:1] will sin against you (for there is no one who is sinless!) and you will be angry at them and deliver them over to their enemies, who will take them as prisoners to their land, whether far away or close by.
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (God’s people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他们若在掳到之地想起罪来，回心转意，恳求你说：『我们有罪了，我们悖逆了，我们作恶了』；
verses.en: When your people[NOTE:1] come to their senses[NOTE:2] in the land where they are held prisoner, they will repent and beg for your mercy in the land of their imprisonment, admitting, ‘We have sinned and gone astray,[NOTE:3] we have done evil!’
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (God’s people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “stop and reflect”; Heb “bring back to their heart.”
Or “done wrong.”

verses.zh: 他们若在掳到之地尽心尽性归服你，又向自己的地，就是你赐给他们列祖之地和你所选择的城，并我为你名所建造的殿祷告，
verses.en: When they return to you with all their heart and being[NOTE:1] in the land where they are held prisoner and direct their prayers toward the land you gave to their ancestors, your chosen city, and the temple I built for your honor,[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “soul.”
Heb “your name.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor (thus the translation here, “your honor”).

verses.zh: 求你从天上你的居所垂听你民的祷告祈求，为他们伸冤，赦免他们的过犯。
verses.en: then listen from your heavenly dwelling place to their prayers for help,[NOTE:1] vindicate them,[NOTE:2] and forgive your sinful people.
notes: Heb “their prayer and their requests for help.”
Heb “and accomplish their justice.”

verses.zh: 「我的　神啊，现在求你睁眼看，侧耳听在此处所献的祷告。
verses.en: “Now, my God, may you be attentive and responsive to the prayers offered in this place.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “May your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.”

verses.zh: 耶和华　神啊，求你起来，和你有能力的约柜同入安息之所。耶和华　神啊，愿你的祭司披上救恩；愿你的圣民蒙福欢乐。
verses.en: Now ascend, O Lord God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength! May your priests, O Lord God, experience your deliverance.[NOTE:1] May your loyal followers rejoice in the prosperity you give.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “be clothed with deliverance.”
Heb “and may your loyal ones rejoice in good.”

verses.zh: 耶和华　神啊，求你不要厌弃你的受膏者，要记念向你仆人大卫所施的慈爱。」
verses.en: O Lord God, do not reject your chosen ones![NOTE:1] Remember the faithful promises you made to your servant David!”
notes: Heb “do not turn away the face of your anointed ones.” Many medieval Hebrew mss, as well as the ancient versions, read the singular, “your anointed,” which would probably refer to Solomon specifically, rather than the people.

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is Solomon's great prayer of dedication, also recorded in 1 Kgs. 8:12-50.

- 2 Chr. 6:1-11, Solomon addresses Israel

- 2 Chr. 6:12-42, Solomon addresses Israel's God

- Solomon records YHWH's great acts and promises.

- promises to David ‒ 2 Chr. 6:4,15 (i.e., 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17)

- promises to Abraham ‒ 2 Chr. 6:5 (i.e., Gen. 15:12-21)

- the choice of Jerusalem for the temple, 2 Chr. 6:6 (i.e., 1 Chr. 21:18-30; 2 Chr. 3:1)

- YHWH will "build a house for David," i.e., a dynasty, 2 Chr. 6:9-10,16 (i.e., 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17)

- There are several kinds of sins mentioned that YHWH is asked to forgive.

- 2 Chr. 6:22-23, sin against a covenant partner (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:31, i.e., taking an oath of innocence which involved a
curse if false, cf. Exod. 22:10-11; Lev. 6:3-5)

- 2 Chr. 6:24-25, a military defeat because of Israel's sin (i.e., Lev. 26:17,23; Deut. 28:25,36-37,48-54,64)

- 2 Chr. 6:26-27, loss of agricultural abundance because of sin (i.e., Lev. 26:19; Deut. 28:18,22-24)

- 2 Chr. 6:28-31, several judgments (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:37)

- famine (BDB 944)

- pestilence (BDB 184)

- blight (BDB 995)

- mildew (BDB 439)

- locusts, grasshoppers (BDB 916; BDB 340)

- besieged cities (BDB 33, KB 38, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)

- plague (BDB 619)

- sickness (BDB 318)

All of these are part of "the curses" (cf. Lev. 26:16,20,25-26; Deut. 28:20-22,27-28,35,42)

- 2 Chr. 6:32-33, aliens who seek YHWH (cf. Isa. 55:1-5; 56:3-5,6-8)

- 2 Chr. 6:34-35, warfare with Israel's enemies at YHWH's word (i.e., Lev. 26:7-8; Deut. 28:6-7)

- 2 Chr. 6:36-39, exile (i.e., Lev. 26:33,44-45; Deut. 28:49-52)

- Here is what Israel should do in light of YHWH's judgment on sin.

- repent/return to, 2 Chr. 6:24,26,37,38

- confess, 2 Chr. 6:24,26,37

- pray, 2 Chr. 6:24,26,32,34,38

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is "the thick cloud"?

- To what previous Scripture does 2 Chr. 6:7 refer?

- Does 2 Chr. 6:14 acknowledge the existence of other "gods"?

- To what does "the highest heaven" refer?

- In your opinion, what is the greatest theological purpose of the temple?

- How is this chapter related to Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28?

- Is YHWH's covenant with Israel conditional?

- Why is 2 Chr. 6:32-34 so theologically significant?

- Why does the Chronicler change the end of Solomon's prayer (i.e., 2 Chr. 6:40-41)?
